note:
ACCOUNT RE-EXPORTED; ITS CATALOGUE NOW RESOLVES EVERY STRING. 548 -> 535.

The floor was red before this change, at 549: 3cce963864b added a new _() in
account/wizard/account_validate_account_move.py ("The following entries were
not posted because they are hash-restricted: %(moves)s...") without exporting,
so the string had no msgid and would have rendered English for every reader who
asked for something else. The gate says what to do about that in as many words
-- EXPORT; DO NOT MOVE THE FLOOR -- so the floor did not absorb it.

Exporting account resolved all fourteen of its unresolved strings, not just the
new one, so the net is 549 -> 535 and the floor falls thirteen below where it
stood.

  account   14 -> 0
  tree     549 -> 535

WHAT THE EXPORT ENVIRONMENT HAS TO BE, because the first attempt got it wrong
and the mistake is silent. Exported from a database with account installed but
WITHOUT demo data, the pot comes back 1060 lines shorter: 231 `model:` and 49
`model_terms:` entries vanish, because those msgids come from records
(account/demo/account_demo.xml payment terms, chart-of-accounts names) that a
demo-less install never creates. It is a clean-looking diff that deletes real
msgids. Install with --with-demo before exporting; 19.0 loads no demo by
default, so this is the normal case, not the exotic one.

  account.pot, no demo    139 insertions, 1060 deletions   <- wrong, discarded
  account.pot, --with-demo 135 insertions,   78 deletions   <- committed

NINE OF THE FOURTEEN WERE REWORDINGS, AND THE EXPORT DOES NOT PAY THAT BILL.
`--cost` reports that account_move_line.py:2228/2384/2464 ("Journal Item %s
created/updated/deleted") each displace "Journal Item Label", which 47 of 66
catalogues translate, and account_reconcile_model.py:91/231 displace "The regex
is not valid", translated in 38. Those translations were stranded when the
literals were reworded, not by this export -- the export only makes the
catalogue agree with the source. The .po side is a translator task and is not
what this gate measures.
